items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: there would be a group standing in front of Jim Robinson, who would be listening to him play his solo parts

ctx.x: What about the reaction of the crowd up there, to the music, uh, other than the dancing? What did they do?

Well, there would be a, uh, a large group usually standing right in front of the bandstand, which was, uh, pretty high up off the floor. I think the bandstand was about, uh, four, three or four feet up, off the floor. And, uh, maybe even more than that. Well, about four feet. And, uh, we'd all be standing there. I would be one of the, one of the crowd standing in front of the bandstand, and looking up at various, uh, idols, you know. And, uh, during a good deal of this time, there was, uh, dissension in the band.…
What would they do at the end of the number? People, what would their reaction be?

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: then George would, uh, come in for a solo usually with Jim, the two of them.

ctx.x: I was going to say, one night, uh, Sidney, uh, Boucher came in, uh, that was 19, uh, the, uh, January of 1946. It had been almost a year since they'd been in Boston together, but they hadn't forgotten any of it. And, but Sidney came up to the Stuyvesant to hear him one night and sat at the table. And Bunk really perked up then and really played about the best of any time. I think I heard him at the Stuyvesant, possibly. One of the best nights he ever had. And he kept the horn pointed right at Sidney then too,…

Well, now Bunk had his, had his own way of playing, uh, these tunes. He, uh, particularly with the Stuyvesant band, he'd, uh, uh, he'd play a couple ensembles in and then, uh, then George would, uh, come in for a solo usually with Jim, the two of them. And Bunk might even keep playing real quietly. I used to get real close to the, to the horn. He'd point the horn down at the floor. And sometimes he'd just be moving the valves and I knew he was playing something and if only I could hear it. And I don't know, it…
Without anybody else taking the straight melody.
